audit: Immediate area around proposed September 2026 White Sox Railyards stadium
scope: Stadium first, immediate surroundings second, skyline only where it frames the outfield

review_method.interaction: Dedicated Chrome tab; source and detailed-v2 render viewed side by side and with opacity overlay
review_method.coordinate_note: Source boxes are approximate native-pixel regions for review targeting, not surveyed geometry. Native sizes: north 1944x1294, south 5000x3333, bridge 1440x959, plan 1948x1190.

calibration_evidence.interpretation: Selected-control fit only; it is not a whole-scene fidelity score.

reference_backed: Visible silhouettes, roof corners, facade bay rhythms, sign placement, river/rail/road relationships, bridge presence, public-realm levels and visible planting/furniture patterns in the supplied images.
North aerial roof-corner footprints for the four named adjacent masses, as recorded in scene-spec.json.
inferred_or_unverified: Absolute building heights, construction assemblies, hidden elevations, exact capacity, exact pavement widths, planting species, below-grade structure and future-development phasing.
The site plan is schematic; its stadium glyph is not a dimensioned footprint. The model records a 3.7-4.7 m affine registration residual and an additional inferred 33 m east-west adjustment.

priority_order: P0: Re-establish source silhouette and facade/cornice identity of the stadium, including the CF rounded frontage and the tower/canopy junction.
P0: Replace generic adjacent masses with the four visible reference buildings and their roof/terrace rhythms.
P1: Build the riverwalk, public stairs, park levels, paths, planting and furniture as a connected public realm.
P1: Correct rail crossings and Roosevelt bridge structure so crossings read as infrastructure rather than thin bars.
P2: Match warm lighting and reduce generic skyline detail until immediate geometry is stable.

elements.label: Stadium envelope, upper canopy, facade rhythm and tower junction
elements.reference_backed: Visible in all three perspective renderings; north bowl outline is the strongest constrained view.

north.focus: Full bowl, left-field tower, canopy and river-facing frontage

south.focus: River-facing brick facade, continuous dark cornice and rail-adjacent bowl

bridge.focus: Bowl silhouette, tower, canopy and external concourse

source_contract: Asymmetric baseball bowl with a broad, continuous dark canopy wrapping the upper decks.
River-facing exterior uses tall, repeated brick bays, a strong horizontal cornice/cap and a lower arcade/glazed concourse.
Clock tower is a legible stacked brick/stone vertical marker with multiple clock faces and a lantern-like top; its base meets the bowl/canopy at a visible corner.
Canopy reads as a structural roof plane with repeated ribs/seams, not a smooth generic band.
current_v2: North field/bowl alignment is visually close in the overlay, but the facade is a procedural repetitive shell and the roof is too smooth and uniformly light.
South and bridge views show the bowl and river-facing frontage as smaller/less dominant than the source; the current context competes with the stadium.
Tower exists and reads at a distance, but its stack, roof junction and adjacent lantern lack the source's architectural weight.
correction_spec: Lock field and north bowl footprint first; treat the calibrated north result as the anchor and fit south/bridge camera or shared geometry only after the anchor survives.

Add a measured facade module: tall brick piers, recessed dark glazing, a distinct upper cornice band, and a lower glazed/arched arcade. Vary bay widths at corners and around entries instead of repeating one bay.
Break the canopy into a visible ribbed surface with a darker underside and a sharper roof-to-wall edge; retain the four separated decks.
Widen/step the tower shaft and make the lantern/cap connection explicit in the silhouette.
elements.confidence: high for silhouette/rhythm; medium for dimensions

elements.label: Northwestern Medicine medical main and wing
elements.reference_backed: North aerial provides a distinctive purple Northwestern Medicine sign and roof/wing relationship; south view repeats the sign building in the rail-side context.

north.focus: Purple Northwestern Medicine sign, long lit facade, roof garden/terrace and wing

south.focus: White/stone medical mass with purple sign beside the rail corridor

bridge.focus: Left-side river context where the medical/rail-side mass is visible only in part

source_contract: Long, horizontally composed clinical building with a legible purple sign band; glazing is finer-grained than the entertainment buildings.
Main and wing masses step in plan and height; roof contains visible planted or mechanical zones rather than one undifferentiated slab.
Building sits across/along the rail and pedestrian connection, so its ground edge participates in the crossing sequence.
current_v2: The named Medical main/wing footprints exist in scene-spec.json, but the detailed render reads as generic gridded blocks; the sign is not legible at comparison scale.
Roof treatment and mass hierarchy do not reproduce the source sign building's stepped, institutional identity; current glazing is too evenly distributed.
correction_spec: Preserve the recorded footprints as the plan prior, then split the mass into a taller main bar and lower wing with a visible step at their joint.
Reserve a high-contrast purple sign panel on the source-facing facade; make it readable in north and south cameras without inventing extra branding.
Use narrower vertical medical curtain-wall bays, stone/aluminum spandrels and a roof garden/mechanical setback; suppress generic rooftop boxes where they do not appear in the source.
elements.confidence: high for sign and mass relationship; medium for roof depth/height

elements.label: Left-field pavilion
elements.reference_backed: North aerial roof corners and visible south/bridge roof silhouette; exact footprint is explicitly marked inferred in scene-spec.json.

north.focus: Dark-roof pavilion between bowl, rail crossing and adjacent hall

south.focus: Rail-side pavilion/roof anchor; selected LF roof control is the largest south residual

bridge.focus: Pavilion mass immediately right of bowl in bridge view

source_contract: A low-to-mid-rise, elongated pavilion mass with a dark, stepped or sloped roof and a strong edge along the rail/crossing zone.
The pavilion mediates between stadium seating, pedestrian deck and the larger hall; it should not read as a free-standing square box.
current_v2: Current render shows a near-cube gridded block at the anchor, with a flat roof and weak connection to the stadium/rail landing.
The LF pavilion selected control has 111.2 px reference error in the south fit, the largest selected residual; this is a useful correction target, not proof of a camera-only error.
correction_spec: Rebuild as an elongated bar aligned to the source roof corners, with a lower concourse base and a darker stepped roof volume.
Add a visible covered landing/bridge connection and keep its height below the medical tower and stadium tower in all three views.
Recheck the south camera after moving the shared mass; the north and bridge images should preserve the roof corner alignment.
elements.confidence: medium; roof corners are visible but elevation and hidden footprint are inferred

elements.label: North entertainment hall
elements.reference_backed: North aerial roof corners and the long lit hall facade are clear; bridge/south views show its brick hall and active roof edge.

north.focus: Long brick/glass hall, rooftop terrace, garden furniture and active park edge

south.focus: Long hall mass immediately beyond stadium/right riverwalk

bridge.focus: Brick hall in stadium's right foreground

source_contract: Long, 4-5 story brick/glass hall with a strong vertical bay cadence, deep roof terrace, visible planting and activity.
Hall forms one edge of the park and connects to the stadium concourse; its ground plane is porous and lit.
Its roof/terrace is a horizontal counterweight to the curved stadium frontage.
current_v2: Current v2 has the named footprint and a generic rectangular block, but the flat slab roof, uniform window grid and blank lawn edge erase the terrace/park relationship.
Current lighting is cold and broad; the hall does not carry the warm window/terrace emphasis seen in the source.
correction_spec: Keep the inferred footprint but model a stepped podium, taller central hall bar and setback rooftop terrace with low parapet.
Use larger vertical bays at the public-facing facade, recessed dark glazing and a brick base; introduce only the visible terrace planting/furniture patterns.
Connect the hall directly to the park path and stadium concourse with a legible threshold and stair/ramp sequence.
elements.confidence: high for visible facade/terrace relationship; medium for exact height

elements.label: Centerfield rounded restaurant / river-facing terrace
elements.reference_backed: Distinctive curved, river-facing frontage below the centerfield board is visible in north, south and bridge views.

north.focus: Rounded glazed frontage below THE RAILYARDS/CF screen with terrace activity

south.focus: Curved front facade and sign/board relationship

bridge.focus: Bright rounded river-side terrace immediately below CF board

source_contract: Broad rounded or semicircular river-facing frontage with a dark curved roof/board assembly above it.
Glazing and vertical structure wrap the curve; upper terrace furniture and people make it an active venue.
The building anchors the riverwalk and the stadium's public front, rather than sitting as a small detached object.
current_v2: The current cylinder is recognizable but underscaled, isolated and too white/bright; its dark canopy/board relationship and upper terrace are weak.
Facade-detail render shows a procedural low cylinder and sparse furniture where the source reads as a broad active frontage.
correction_spec: Increase the curved frontage to the source's visible width relative to the CF board; keep a short straight wing only where the source indicates one.
Wrap a consistent dark canopy/cornice over the curve, add glazed vertical mullion rhythm and a readable lower arcade/entry band.
Place a compact upper terrace with visible tables/umbrellas and connect it to the river promenade with steps and a broad landing; avoid arbitrary extra floors.
elements.confidence: high for silhouette and placement; medium for exact radius

elements.label: Rail corridor, visible rail crossings and covered pedestrian decks
elements.reference_backed: Rail tracks and multiple cross-rail decks are visible in all aerial references and in the plan; exact operating rail geometry is outside the supplied evidence.

north.focus: Rail yard, multiple covered crossings and stadium-side landings

south.focus: Long parallel tracks, repeated road/pedestrian bridges and underpasses

bridge.focus: Rail corridor and crossing structures behind/left of stadium

plan.focus: Rail corridor west of stadium and repeated cross-site connections

source_contract: Several parallel tracks form a deep corridor west of the stadium; crossings occur at repeated intervals and have substantial deck width, guard/roof edges and landings.
Pedestrian decks are covered or visually substantial, linking the stadium concourse to the medical/pavilion/hall side.
Road and rail crossings are layered; the source does not read as a few isolated horizontal bars.
current_v2: Four crossing objects are present in r2_district.py at y=-113,-48,73,150, but current renders show thin, repetitive gray decks with weak landings and little depth.
Track bed is a dark straight trench; the source has denser track/bridge layering and richer edge conditions.
correction_spec: Keep the four crossings as a count prior, then give each a source-like covered deck, opaque side/roof edge, guardrails and widened concourse landing.
Tie deck elevation to the rail trench and stadium ground levels; show at least one clear stair/ramp drop at each public landing.
Retain simplified rails, but add visible parallel tracks, sleepers and road/bridge hierarchy before adding distant buildings.
elements.confidence: high for crossing presence/count class; medium for exact widths and levels

elements.label: River edge, riverwalk width and level changes
elements.reference_backed: River edge is visible in the three perspectives and the site plan; level widths are visual estimates.

north.focus: River-facing promenade, quay wall, stairs and boats

south.focus: River channel, linear promenade and crossings

bridge.focus: Both banks, water-level structure and foreground public realm

plan.focus: River alignment and bends around the site

source_contract: Promenade is broad enough for crowds and terraces; river edge includes a hard quay plus lower/water-adjacent level in places.
Stairs descend from upper plaza/park levels to the lower walk; railings follow the edge but are subordinate to the public space.
River channel and banks bend toward the 18th Street area in the plan/source context; width is not uniform.
current_v2: Current model uses straight parallel quays, a largely single-level riverwalk and narrow strips; the source's stepped depth and active width are absent.
Current railings and stairs are present in code but are too subtle or hidden in perspective renders; the lower edge does not read as a deliberate public level.
correction_spec: Build upper concourse, intermediate terrace and lower riverwalk as separate slabs with a visible 1.5-3 m level difference as an inferred visual prior.
Widen the stadium-side walk and vary it at the rounded restaurant/park edge; add broad stair flights at the visible source locations, with ramps where a continuous route is implied.
Keep the river simplified, but introduce the source's bend/variable bank alignment south of Roosevelt and avoid a constant-width canal abstraction.
elements.confidence: high for multi-level/width relationship; medium for absolute dimensions

elements.label: Park shape, paths, stairs, planting and furniture
elements.reference_backed: North aerial and bridge view clearly show the central lawn/park, paths, tree clusters, seating and crowd zones; site plan supports the public-realm placement.

north.focus: Large lawn, diagonal paths, tree clusters, benches/tables and hall edge

south.focus: Stadium-side plazas, lawns, linear planting and crowd paths

bridge.focus: Lit lawn/park between hall, stadium and Roosevelt bridge

plan.focus: Open-space bands and connections around the stadium glyph

source_contract: Park is an irregular connected lawn/plaza system with diagonal and orthogonal paths, not one blank rectangle.
Planting is grouped along edges and in loose clusters; trees vary in spacing and are integrated with seating/crowd zones.
Source shows tables, benches, umbrellas, lights and dense pedestrian activity near the hall, restaurant and river edge.
Stairs and broad landings visibly stitch upper park and lower riverwalk levels.
current_v2: Current park is a large blank green rectangle with a grid of evenly spaced trees and little furniture; path hierarchy is hard to read from north or bridge views.
Procedural benches, lights and two simple stair bands exist but do not establish the source's park shape or level sequence.
Current visitor placements are dense in some linear bands but lack the source's clear event/courtyard clustering.
correction_spec: Replace the single rectangular lawn with 2-4 connected lawn and paved rooms, using the hall and river edges as hard boundaries.
Lay out one primary diagonal walk, one river-parallel walk and short cross-links; widen entries at the rounded restaurant, hall and bridge landings.
Use irregular tree clusters and continuous planted edges with varied spacing; add a small, repeated furniture kit only in visible source zones.
Make the stair/landing geometry legible in north and bridge cameras before increasing pedestrian count.
elements.confidence: high for public-realm pattern; medium for exact planting/furniture inventory

elements.label: Roosevelt bridge structure and nearby context
elements.reference_backed: Bridge view gives the clearest source evidence; plan confirms Roosevelt crossing north of the stadium.

north.focus: Roosevelt/upper rail-side approach only partly visible

south.focus: Road/rail crossing context near the upper site

bridge.focus: Broad multi-lane foreground deck, paired towers/pylons, under-span and riverwalk

plan.focus: Roosevelt Rd crossing and river bridge north of site

source_contract: Broad multi-lane road deck spans the river in the foreground; source shows traffic, lane rhythm and substantial parapets.
Two prominent bridge-edge tower/pylon or tender-house forms with rounded/ornamental tops are visible, one on each bank/road edge.
Under-span structure includes a clearly visible lower arch/steel assembly and water-level relationship; adjacent riverwalk continues below/along the bridge.
Bridge context includes dense park lighting and trees on the near/right bank.
current_v2: Current bridge renders as a narrow/simple deck with repetitive thin truss members, box piers and small tender houses; the source's paired ornamental forms and under-span depth are missing.
Current road/traffic scale is subdued and the adjacent riverwalk lawn is too blank to support the bridge composition.
correction_spec: Match deck width and height first, then add two source-facing tower/pylon silhouettes at the bank/road-edge positions; keep their ornament simple but unmistakable.
Model a separate under-span steel/arch assembly and bank abutments so the river opening reads as layered structure.
Add lane markings, parapets, traffic and bridge lighting at source density; connect the right-bank park and lower walk beneath the bridge.
elements.confidence: high for bridge width/tower/under-span presence; medium for structural type

elements.label: Skyline and future-development context beyond the outfield
elements.reference_backed: South and bridge references show a dense future skyline; north reference is primarily stadium/low-rise context.

north.focus: Low-rise context beyond the outfield and medical district

south.focus: Dense warm skyline framing stadium from south

bridge.focus: Low horizon and a few towers behind outfield

source_contract: Skyline is a framing layer beyond the stadium; its density and height differ by source view.
Immediate adjacent buildings remain legible in front of the skyline and should carry the near-field identity.
current_v2: South current render is dominated by generic procedural high-rises and a pale horizon; the current blocks do not match the source's warm density.
Bridge current render leaves excessive empty sky and generic low-rise context, while the stadium and bridge are still underfit.
The gallery correctly labels future development and distant city as inferred; these layers should not drive near-field corrections.
correction_spec: Freeze skyline work until P0/P1 immediate geometry is stable. Keep future development separable and view-specific.
When revisited, use broad height/density silhouettes and source warm value structure only beyond the outfield; avoid claiming building identities from the concept art.
elements.confidence: high for priority/deprioritization; low for skyline identity

overall_assessment.stadium: North bowl and field placement are the strongest part of v2, but facade/cornice, tower junction, canopy ribs and rounded CF frontage remain visibly schematic.
overall_assessment.immediate_area: The four adjacent masses, riverwalk levels, park geometry, rail crossings and Roosevelt bridge are the main fidelity gap; current geometry reads as generic blocks and straight infrastructure.
overall_assessment.skyline: Current skyline is sufficient as an inferred placeholder and should remain third priority until near-field elements are corrected.
overall_assessment.do_not_overclaim: The audit is a visual reconstruction review against concept renderings and a schematic plan. It does not establish surveyed dimensions, engineering structure, official phasing or recognition accuracy.
